key_insight: A 44.8M-parameter transformer can synthesize quantum circuits well when post-processing can correct errors, but exact discrete synthesis on Clifford+T circuits breaks down as autoregressive drift compounds across longer outputs.
engineering_relevance: For fault-tolerant quantum compilers, the result shows that exact equivalence is the bottleneck—not syntax or coarse resource prediction—and that inference-time search and more data are practical levers for improving reliability.
method: Encoder-decoder transformer with structured circuit tokenization
Hybrid synthesis for parameterized circuits: transformer proposes structure, classical optimization refines angles
Exact Clifford+T circuit generation evaluated with equivalence verification and candidate reranking
evidence_signal: On parameterized circuits the hybrid method reached median fidelity 1.000, while on Clifford+T circuits exact-match accuracy fell from 88% for circuits with <=9 gates to near zero beyond 26 gates; reranking improved exact matches from 7% to 22.5%, and 2.5x more training data raised them to 39.5%.
watch_item: The main limitation is length-sensitive autoregressive drift, so even stronger models may still fail on long exact circuits unless decoding is made more robust or verification is integrated tightly.
paper_title: When Close Enough Is Not Enough: Autoregressive Drift in Quantum Circuit Synthesis
